public_holidays: No state-only statutory public holidays: Austria's public holidays are national and are on Austria's record.
culture-cycles.note: The patron-saint day is a school holiday in this state. The ministry lists it apart from the statutory public holidays, so do not assume shops or businesses close; the ministry page does not say.

laws.rule: Drinking alcohol is banned at Praterstern (station and stop areas, access routes, the neighbouring public roads and green areas, and the Venediger-Au-Park), under a City of Vienna ordinance published in the city gazette on 26 April 2018. Carrying alcohol openly in a way that shows drinking is about to happen counts as drinking (for example opening a container). Customers of licensed venues during opening hours and approved events are excepted. Breaking it is an administrative offence with a fine and forfeiture of the drinks; officers may ask to inspect the containers and dispose of opened ones. The ordinance does not state the fine amount.
laws.heading: Verordnung des Magistrates der Stadt Wien, Verbot des Konsumierens von alkoholischen Getränken am Praterstern (Amtsblatt Nr. 17, 26 April 2018)

laws.rule: The City of Vienna's press service (27 April 2026) describes an alcohol consumption ban zone at Westbahnhof: Europaplatz, the area around the Wiener Linien station building, Helga-Pollak-Kinsky-Park and Christian-Broda-Platz. The release does not give a start date, hours or fine, so check the city gazette for the ordinance before relying on it.
laws.heading: Stadt Wien, Presse-Service, 27 April 2026

laws.rule: Vienna's visitor tax (Ortstaxe) is 5% of the price paid for the stay, not counting VAT and a usual breakfast charge, under sections 12 and 14 of the Wiener Tourismusförderungsgesetz. It applies to every paying guest in any kind of accommodation in the city, including when a third party pays. Hosts collect it and pay it to the city by the 15th of the following month (section 13).
laws.heading: Wiener Tourismusförderungsgesetz, sections 11 to 14

laws.rule: Vienna: Curfew for minors in public places and at public events (the Jugendschutz rule): young people up to the end of their 14th year may be out only from 05:00 to 23:00, and up to the end of their 16th year only from 05:00 to 01:00, unless they have an accompanying person or a justified reason such as heading home (section 8(1) and (2) of the Wiener Jugendschutzgesetz 2002).
laws.heading: Wiener Jugendschutzgesetz 2002, section 8

laws.rule: Vienna: under 16, buying, having or drinking alcohol in public places, public facilities and at public events is banned; under 18 the same applies to drinks containing distilled alcohol (spirits). Giving such drinks to them is also banned (section 11a of the Wiener Jugendschutzgesetz 2002).
laws.heading: Wiener Jugendschutzgesetz 2002, section 11a

laws.rule: Vienna: under 18, buying, having or using nicotine products, tobacco, water pipes, e-cigarettes and e-shishas in public places, public facilities and at public events is banned, and using them in schools (section 11(1) of the Wiener Jugendschutzgesetz 2002).
laws.heading: Wiener Jugendschutzgesetz 2002, section 11

laws.rule: In Vienna's green land zone (Grünland) it is banned to camp, or to set up and use caravans, motorhomes or mobile homes, except on camping grounds and on garden-type land next to homes (section 17(2)(2) of the Wiener Naturschutzgesetz). The fine scale was not read.
laws.heading: Wiener Naturschutzgesetz, section 17(2)
